description: An S3 bucket exposed to the internet in two ways. PublicAssetBucket declares no PublicAccessBlockConfiguration, so nothing at the bucket level prevents a policy or an ACL from making its objects public. PublicAssetBucketPolicy then does exactly that: an Allow statement with Principal "*" granting s3:GetObject on every object, with no Condition. The bucket is otherwise correctly configured -- server-side encryption, server access logging to a parameterised destination bucket, Environment and Owner tags -- so the encryption, logging and tagging rules have nothing to report and the case measures public access only.

expected_findings.note: No PublicAccessBlockConfiguration on the bucket, reported by the s3_public_access_block Guard rule.

Principal "*" granted s3:GetObject on every object in the bucket policy, with no Condition. Reported by the principal_star IAM detector; the category is IAM because that is the category every Layer 1 IAM detector assigns.
